hardware_summary: All-electric "Compact E-Drive" design: electric motor drive technology (~700 MW total) for all liquefaction process and utility compressors, pumps and fans, powered by BC Hydro via a new ~16 km, 16 kV/high-voltage overhead transmission line from the Minette Substation to the Bish Cove plant site. On-site generation is limited to four 2.5 MW, 13.8 kV DIESEL-powered back-up generation units for essential power during emergencies/critical loads only - the filing explicitly states this design "reduc[es] the need for an onsite natural gas-powered generation facility."
fuel_basis: Primary power: none on-site (BC Hydro grid electricity). On-site backup only: diesel (not natural gas) - fails the captive-GAS-power fuel gate.
captive_summary: Chevron Canada Limited's own 2019 BC EAO Amendment #3 filing (the Kitimat LNG/KM LNG Expansion Project, a.k.a. Compact E-Drive design) explicitly states the terminal purchases power from the BC Hydro grid via a dedicated new transmission line, explicitly reducing the need for an on-site natural-gas-fired generation facility; the only on-site generation is diesel-fired emergency backup, which does not meet the captive-GAS-power fuel gate.
confirmed_how: Located via the BC Environmental Assessment Office (EAO) public project registry (projects.eao.gov.bc.ca, project code kitimat-lng-terminal, id 588510cdaaecd9001b815f84) - the 2019 "Kitimat LNG Project Description Amendment 3" filing (document id 5d278561caf02f00216ee6ab), an official Chevron Canada Limited engineering document filed with the regulator, explicitly describing the all-electric compact-drive design, BC Hydro grid supply, new transmission line from Minette Substation, and diesel-only on-site backup generation (4x2.5MW).

hardware_summary: Proposed on-site "Power Generation Facility" train comprising gas turbines, steam turbines, a heat recovery steam generator, and electrical generators, sized at up to ~500 MW per 12 mtpa build-out phase (up to ~1,000 MW at full 24 mtpa build-out); fed by natural gas diverted from the terminal's own feed-gas pipeline supply (~5-7% of throughput) plus recovered boil-off/end-flash gas as fuel gas. fuel_basis: Natural gas - both pipeline feed gas (diverted ~5-7% of throughput) and recovered boil-off/end-flash gas are explicitly named as the power generation facility's fuel.
